The spirometry and X-ray confirm your COPD, but the new dry cough and recent stroke require us to rule out a pulmonary embolism or aspiration. Have you recently experienced any leg swelling or pain, or any sudden onset of shortness of breath while resting?

REQUEST TEST: D-Dimer. Additionally, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or a sensation of food sticking in your throat recently?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pulmonary Embolism secondary to Ischemic Stroke (Post-stroke dysphagia/aspiration risk). The normal D-dimer is a false negative in high-risk patients (stroke), and the stroke history combined with exertional dyspnea and dry cough strongly suggests an embolic event despite the initial negative screening.
